fact: TTCL's Director General said in November 2025 that 11 international submarine cable connections already terminate through Dar es Salaam and Mombasa, including SEACOM, EASSy and 2Africa (count spans both ports; the document does not split it between Tanzania and Kenya).

Airtel Tanzania activated the 2Africa subsea cable landing station at Mbezi, Dar es Salaam, reported 24 September 2024 (officials spoke 23 September; activation date between June and September 2024 per source note).

SDxCentral reported that the Airtel 2Africa Marine Cable Centre in Dar es Salaam was launched in the week of 15 August 2023 at an event attended by the President, as the East African portion of 2Africa went live.

African Business says international traffic reaches Dar es Salaam via several subsea cables, and that Wingu's Dar es Salaam data centre has direct access to the SEACOM, EASSy and 2Africa cables; 2Africa has added bandwidth though some sections are still to be completed (article date used).

The Citizen reports Tanzania is linked to the SEACOM, EASSy and expanding 2Africa submarine cable systems, and that submarine cables land in Dar es Salaam (all at one city, so two routes, not independent; article date used).
The April 2022 Axian-led acquisition of Tigo Tanzania and Zantel gave Axian strategic ownership in the EASSy cable landing station in Dar es Salaam, per Axian/Connecting Africa.
The 2016 National ICT Policy says the cost of internet access fell by over 50 percent in 2010 with the landing of two submarine cables in Dar es Salaam, EASSy and SEACOM (same city, so two routes).
Minister Kairuki said in a 18 July 2026 speech that Tanzania has four submarine cable stations (vituo vinne vya mikongo ya bahari), without naming the cables or stations.
Daily News, citing TCRA data, reports that international fibre optic submarine cables landing in Tanzania rose from two to three between March 2021 and December 2025, without naming them.
The Horohoro redundancy route launched with Kenya gives Tanzania a land path to eight undersea cables via Kenya, alongside its three marine cable connections in Dar es Salaam, per Minister Silaa.

Paratus Tanzania says its new Dar es Salaam PoP gives Tanzania access to Paratus-owned network routes north to Nairobi via Mombasa and south to Maputo, with direct international connectivity to Europe and the US.
